reasoning: Step 1: Selected TL-IN-76101000 as the best description match for 'aluminium window frames' among the three candidates; no HS code conflict, so confidence high.
Step 2: The chosen line has CEPA status PREFERENTIAL with a 2026 CEPA rate of 0%, so preference applies.
Step 3: MFN rate is 10% (tariff and effective both 10%), preferential rate is 0% under India-UAE CEPA.
Step 4: Rule PSR-IN-R118 requires CTSH + VA 45%; origin check status is INSUFFICIENT_DATA, so no checks run and missing documents prevent qualification.
Step 5: Duty calculation status is NEEDS_VALUE because no shipment value was provided; only rate difference of 10 percentage points is available.

Step 6: Since origin status is NEEDS_MORE_DATA, procedure steps include factory registration, applying for the certificate of origin via the Ministry of Foreign Trade's e-service, paying the fee (AED 10-200), and the Indian importer claiming the rate at filing.
Step 7: Key caveats include the '+' interpretation, undefined labour/overhead costs, free-zone ineligibility risk, and the fact that CEPA reduces BCD only.

classification.description: Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium)

origin_result.basis: No checks run; missing a bill of materials (each input's description, 6-digit HS code, origin country, value and currency) and a declaration (product price, FOB or Ex-Works basis, final manufacture in the UAE, operations done in the UAE).

procedure.step: Register the factory through the Ministry of Economy and Tourism's Factory Registration service; the factory must be outside a free zone, hold a MoIAT industrial licence, and have a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added. Registration takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Log in to the Ministry of Foreign Trade's e-services portal.
Choose the Certificate of Origin for India service.
Fill in the application form with the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product.
Upload the required documents: proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and, for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice.
Pay the certificate fee online; the fee depends on the invoice value in AED and ranges from AED 10 to AED 200.
Receive approval, or a return with comments to correct.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, holds origin information under CAROTAR 2020, keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years from filing, and answers any customs request within 10 working days.
The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years starting from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue.

caveats.note: Mansha interprets '+' in the rule as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+'.

Direct labour cost and direct overhead cost are not defined in the agreement, and it is unclear whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty only; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge, and any anti-dumping or safeguard duties still apply.
The certificate of origin must be presented for the CEPA rate to apply.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate; confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources (CBIC Instruction 28/2022 via LiveLaw, taxmann).
The agreement says box 8 for remarks, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.

The Ministry of Foreign Trade offers the e-service that issues preferential and non-preferential certificates of origin for locally made products, but no official page read names it as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically; the India-specific page is still on the Ministry of Economy and Tourism website.

The certificate is valid for 12 months from issue and covers one import; it should be issued before, at, or within 5 working days of export. A certificate may be issued retrospectively up to 12 months from the date of shipment, marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9.
